status_summary: VA proposed on 2025-08-04 and finalized on 2025-12-31 a rule titled Reproductive Health Services (90 FR 61310, effective 2026-01-30). It restores the exclusion of abortion and abortion counseling from the medical benefits package and from CHAMPVA, reversing the 2022 interim final rule and the 2024 final rule. The final rule removes the rape, incest and health-endangerment exceptions; CHAMPVA keeps a life-of-the-mother exception, and VA states that care for life-threatening pregnancy complications remains covered. VA cites a 2025-12-18 Department of Justice Office of Legal Counsel opinion as its primary legal basis. Minority Veterans of America filed a challenge in the Federal Circuit, reported by the Associated Press as filed on or about 2026-05-21, asking the court to throw out the rule; no stay or ruling was found as of 2026-10-26. Separately, on 2025-03-17 VA rescinded VHA Directive 1341(4) on gender dysphoria care, stopped offering cross-sex hormone therapy to new patients (veterans already receiving it from VA, or who received it from the military at separation, may continue), and stated that it has never offered sex-change surgery and will not provide other medical or surgical therapy for gender dysphoria.

timeline.event: VA announces it is rescinding VHA Directive 1341(4), ending cross-sex hormone therapy for new patients with gender dysphoria while allowing current recipients to continue, and states it has never offered sex-change surgery.

uncertainties: The abortion half is well sourced (final rule text read; the 90 FR 36415 and 90 FR 61310 citations, the 2026-01-30 effective date and the 2025-12-18 Office of Legal Counsel opinion date were confirmed on federalregister.gov on 2026-10-26). The Federal Circuit petition is known only through news reports; its docket was not read, so whether a stay was requested or a briefing schedule exists is unknown. A petition copy posted by the petitioner's counsel (National Women's Law Center) and a docket number and filing date from an advocacy litigation report were seen as leads only and are not cited or relied on; the filing date in the timeline is inferred from the Associated Press report, which says the suit was filed on the Thursday before its 2026-05-22 publication. A Federal Register search for VA documents mentioning gender dysphoria returned no VA rule, so the gender care change was made by directive or memo, as the VA release of 2025-03-17 describes. A clearinghouse page shows the 2025 Court of Appeals for Veterans Claims case challenging the gender dysphoria directive rescission closed by voluntary dismissal on 2025-06-23 with no ruling. Rechecked 2026-10-26: a Federal Register query for VA documents titled Reproductive Health Services returned only the 2025-12-31 final rule, the 2025-08-04 proposed rule and the 2024 and 2022 rules, so no amendment or new rule appeared; a news search found no Federal Circuit stay, ruling or briefing report after 2026-05-22. The Mandate's broader scope (all directives contrary to its principles) is undefined. The petition for review itself was read on 2026-10-26 on a copy posted by petitioner's counsel: it is dated 2026-05-15, names no docket number, and asks the Federal Circuit to set aside the 2025-12-31 final rule (90 FR 61310) under 38 U.S.C. 502 as arbitrary and capricious; the Associated Press report places the filing on 2026-05-21, so the filing date is between 2026-05-15 and 2026-05-21 and the docket was not read. The court status rests on the news report of the filing, with the counsel-hosted copy as corroboration; a court-hosted copy or the docket would settle the date and number.
